Some of these men were my friends — but not all. Others were co-workers, acquaintances, the dads of my kids’ classmates. Nor were they necessarily gamers. items.title: IEA Sees Data Center Boom Pushing Power Grids to the Limit
items.content_text: The IEA's World Energy Outlook 2026 projects that AI-driven data center demand could double electricity consumption to 1,000 TWh by 2030. Supply chain constraints for critical equipment and grid expansion speeds are emerging as the primary bottlenecks for scaling AI infrastructure.

items.title: Canva adds an AI ‘off’ button
items.content_text: Canva has introduced an 'off' switch for generative AI features, allowing users to disable tools like Magic Expand and its chatbot while retaining non-generative utilities like background removal. This move responds to user frustration over AI proliferation and introduces filters to limit AI-generated content in search results.

items.title: Germany, Austria Propose Trump-Style Takeover of TikTok’s EU Ops
items.content_text: German Media Minister Wolfram Weimer and Austrian Digital Secretary Alexander Pröll have proposed moving TikTok's European operations under European ownership. The initiative aims to mitigate data security concerns related to its Chinese parent company, ByteDance, mirroring recent forced-divestiture models seen in the US.

items.title: A human liver has been kept alive outside the body for a record seven weeks
items.content_text: Researchers in Australia claim they’ve kept a human liver alive, on life support, outside the body for seven weeks, opening up speculative new possibilities in biomedical engineering. The feat, whose details are pending publication, was carried out in Sydney after a team led by surgeon and inventor Carlo Pulitano connected a donated liver to a system of automated pumps and sensors that fed the organ nutrients, supplied it with blood, and whisked away waste. items.title: Google is forcing Android app developers to properly support foldables
items.content_text: Now that Apple’s foldable is here, Google wants to make sure apps on Android foldables are a good experience. Starting in April 2027, Google is going to require Android developers to make sure their apps have a baseline level of support for foldables. If they don’t, developers risk not being able to publish or update their apps or have reduced visibility for their apps on Google Play. items.content_text: Snapchat announced on Wednesday that it’s giving Lens creators the ability to build Lenses using the AI coding assistants they already use, like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Snapchat Lenses, which are a core part of the social network’s platform, are AR effects that let users alter their appearance, add digital objects to their surroundings, or interact with animated experiences through the camera. items.title: Korea becomes world's 4th country to reach $1 tril. in annual exports
items.content_text: The South Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced that the nation's annual exports hit $1 trillion for the first time, fueled by robust demand for semiconductors and data center infrastructure driven by global AI investment. While full-year projections reach $1.17 trillion, officials warned that potential slowdowns in AI spending, chip price volatility, and trade barriers remain key risks to future momentum.

items.title: European Retail Traders Snag $1.1 Billion of Anthropic IPO Stock
items.content_text: AI lab Anthropic PBC raised $1.1 billion from retail investors in the UK and continental Europe as part of a record-breaking $107.3 billion initial public offering. Despite market concerns regarding the pace of AI spending and market volatility, the company successfully priced its IPO above the marketed range.

items.title: TSMC and Samsung suspend some chip shipments to Chinese customers
items.content_text: TSMC and Samsung Electronics have suspended shipments of certain advanced processors to Chinese customers following new export control rules from the US Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS). The updated regulations remove exemptions previously used to bypass AI-related export restrictions, mandating that foundries must obtain specific US government licenses for advanced manufacturing orders, significantly impacting Chinese AI and consumer electronics companies.

items.title: OCR models now digitize a million pages for under $130 as costs drop fivefold in 18 months
items.content_text: Research from Hugging Face indicates that the cost of large-scale document OCR has dropped fivefold over the past 18 months, driven by lightweight model architectures and improved GPU rental efficiencies. Processing one million pages now costs between $65 and $130 in GPU compute, with newer models achieving parity in accuracy compared to older, more expensive counterparts.

items.title: A profile of Netflix's new Chief Content Officer Peter Rice, a former Fox and Disney executive, as sources say he may focus on revamping its film strategy (Alex Weprin/The Hollywood Reporter)
items.content_text: Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos has appointed former Disney Entertainment Chairman and Fox executive Peter Rice as the new Chief Content Officer, succeeding Bela Bajaria to overhaul the streamer's content strategy. With his proven track record in scaling FX and Hulu, Rice is tasked with shifting Netflix’s output from quantity-driven models toward a mix of commercial viability and high-end prestige productions.

items.title: The Anti-A.I. Campus Movement Is Growing
items.content_text: University students and faculty globally are protesting the integration of generative AI through petitions, religious exemption filings, and manifestos. The movement seeks to curtail institutional partnerships with AI vendors like OpenAI and Google, citing concerns over the erosion of critical thinking and the intrinsic value of human-centric education.

items.title: US companies turn to robots to ease labour shortage crisis
items.content_text: North American manufacturers are accelerating robot adoption to mitigate severe labor shortages, with Q3 2026 orders reaching 11,000 units, a 25% year-on-year increase. Notably, orders for collaborative robots (cobots) surged by 56%, serving as a critical lever for firms to scale output amid persistent workforce limitations.

items.title: Google Ruth Porat Pledges Data Center Local Support Amid Backlash
items.content_text: Alphabet and Google President Ruth Porat announced a $15 billion investment in data center infrastructure in Missouri. The central project, 'Project Spade' in Montgomery County, targets a 1.2GW capacity. To address energy needs, Google is partnering with utility providers Ameren and Evergy to secure 500MW of additional grid capacity while utilizing a Capacity Commitment Framework (CCF) to protect local rate payers.

items.title: Anthropic retail investors face squeeze in blockbuster IPO
items.content_text: Anthropic aims to allocate approximately 20% of its IPO to individual investors, yet the offering has been heavily oversubscribed by institutional demand managed by JPMorgan. Despite efforts through brokers like Robinhood and Fidelity, the significant oversubscription is expected to compress the final retail allocation below the initial 20% target.

items.title: Bloomberg Asia
items.content_text: ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming has become the richest person in Asia with a net worth exceeding $105 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. His wealth surged following valuation markups by institutional investors like BlackRock and Fidelity, coupled with ByteDance's aggressive pivot toward AI development, including Doubao, Seedance, and a massive 10-trillion-parameter model.

items.title: Bloomberg - Business News, Stock Markets, Finance, Breaking & World News
items.content_text: Financial experts, including former SEC Chair Gary Gensler, are warning of a significant speculative bubble in AI stocks. The core concern centers on the widening gap between massive capital expenditures in AI infrastructure and actual generated returns, exacerbated by circular financing and high debt, raising the specter of a market crash.

items.title: I Spent a Year Talking to Anthropic Employees. Here’s What They Believe.
items.content_text: As Anthropic prepares for a landmark IPO, internal concerns regarding the risks of 'recursive self-improvement' have intensified, with staff forecasting the arrival of superhuman AI researchers as early as 2027. Despite internal calls to decelerate development for safety, leadership intends to prioritize the acquisition of compute capacity via IPO proceeds to maintain competitive edge in the race toward autonomous model evolution.

items.title: Lenovo Sales Beat Estimate Due to Solid AI Hardware Demand
items.content_text: Lenovo Group reported a 48% revenue surge in its fiscal second quarter, primarily driven by robust demand for AI infrastructure. The performance exceeded analyst expectations, keeping the company on track to meet its $100 billion annual revenue target.

items.title: China’s military seeks Nvidia chips as US tightens export curbs
items.content_text: The U.S. Department of Commerce has intensified export controls on high-performance AI processors, restricting companies like Nvidia from supplying advanced computing power to China. This strategy aims to curb the deployment of AI in intelligent warfare while forcing Nvidia to navigate a narrow path between stringent regulatory compliance and maintaining its market share.
